FLAGSHIP SPACE PROJECT · RECENT SAUDI SPACE ACADEMY WORK

Automated Orbital Debris Mitigation Framework

Designed as a staged space-safety workflow: read astronomical/space imagery with Astropy CCDData; calibrate imagery through bias, dark and flat correction with ccdproc; identify stronger candidate detections using photutils / DAOStarFinder; then connect detection to Hill relative-motion modeling and an adapted Roche-limit risk boundary to estimate a safer separation zone.

The proposed next-stage expansion is a six-face CubeSat concept: increase imaging coverage across six lenses/faces, evaluate detections from multiple viewing directions, and connect the analysis to the exact satellite FITS imagery and engineering parameters such as size, mass and shape. Backend Python results would then be checked against the web-based implementation for consistency.

HOW THE SPACE WORK CONNECTS

Detection → Relative Motion → Risk Boundary → Multi-Face CubeSat Expansion

The portfolio now reveals the engineering logic rather than only naming the project. Higher-sigma source detections are treated as stronger candidate detections requiring validation, not automatically as collision risk. The orbital stage uses position coordinates x, y, z; relative velocities u, v, w; angular/orbital rate and simulation steps. The proposed risk-boundary stage then uses physical parameters, including density-sensitive Roche-limit inputs, to define a modeled separation region.
